title: SEIU 1000 announces one-day strike in California over contract dispute

tea.why: Protesters cite bad-faith bargaining by the state administration during 2026 contract negotiations and return-to-office mandates.
tea.want: Demanding a 20% salary increase over three years, increased healthcare contributions, and telework options.
tea.changed: Oct 8: SEIU Local 1000 announced a scheduled one-day strike for Oct 21 after members voted 96.2% in favor.

summary: The Service Employees International Union (SEIU) Local 1000 announced a one-day strike scheduled for October 21 following a member vote in which 96.2% authorized the action. The union, representing public sector employees in California, cited alleged bad-faith bargaining by Governor Gavin Newsom's administration during 2026 contract negotiations. Key grievances include wage disputes, healthcare costs, and a mandatory return-to-office order. The planned demonstrations will take place in Sacramento and other cities including Oakland, Fresno, San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Norwalk, and San Bernardino, potentially causing delays in government services such as the DMV. In response, the California Department of Human Resources stated that it remains ready to negotiate a fair agreement while protecting essential services.
demands: A 20% general salary increase over three years
Telework options that work for employees
response: CalHR stated that it remains ready to sit down anytime with the union to negotiate a fair and responsible agreement, while keeping the state focused on protecting essential services for Californians.

updates.text: SEIU 1000 announced a one-day strike for Oct. 21 after 96.2% of voting members authorized the action.
